datasets.title: VisA (Visual Anomaly) — Vision Lens benchmark subset

parts.rationale: Four object classes, chosen for visual distinctness rather than size: candle (multiple instances, 8 anomaly classes), capsules (multiple instances, 5 anomaly classes), fryum (single instance, 8 anomaly classes) and pcb1 (complex PCB structure, 4 anomaly classes). Together they cover both object layouts and both defect granularities, and every class contributes normal and anomalous images in sufficient volume. The upstream release carries 12 classes in total (candle, capsules, cashew, chewinggum, fryum, macaroni1, macaroni2, pcb1-pcb4, pipe_fryum); the other eight are left out to keep the F0 benchmark loop inside the 600-800 image band. Expand the selection by editing this field and re-running the fetch with --parts.

datasets.attribution: Visual Anomaly (VisA), from the Registry of Open Data on AWS: https://registry.opendata.aws/visa. The registry entry, the license and the archive URL were verified on 2026-11-10; the archive itself was fetched on 2026-11-11 (see fetchedAt) and its sha256 was pinned from the received bytes. Zou, Yang, Jongheon Jeong, Latha Pemula, Dongqing Zhang, and Onkar Dabeer. "SPot-the-Difference Self-Supervised Pre-training for Anomaly Detection and Segmentation." arXiv preprint arXiv:2207.14315 (2022).
datasets.notes: Archive: the dated release tarball VisA_20220922.tar (1,929,840,640 bytes) in the S3 bucket amazon-visual-anomaly (us-west-2), served anonymously. The ETag above is recorded as PROVENANCE ONLY: the object is a MULTIPART upload (the trailing -113 is the part count), so its ETag is neither the content MD5 nor a checksum of any kind. The trustworthy digest is the sha256 the fetch script computes from the received bytes; the value above was pinned by the first authorized fetch on 2026-11-11 with --record-checksums. Annotation source: each class directory carries its own image_anno.csv (image,label,mask); the label is the image-level ground truth and maps onto the ontology keys normal | defect:<type> using the dataset's own class taxonomy (amazon-research/spot-diff, utils/id2class.py). Dataset binaries never enter git: datasets/visa-subset/ and datasets/cache/ are ignored.

datasets.title: MVTec AD — research reference only (NOT a benchmark source)

parts.rationale: No parts are selected: this entry documents the reference dataset, it does not fetch it. MVTec AD is the field's classic comparison point for industrial anomaly detection (15 categories, ~5,354 high-resolution images with pixel-precise anomaly masks), but its license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and forbids commercial use. The platform's commercial context therefore rules it out as a benchmark source. It is recorded here so that the research path is explicit and a later, deliberate, license-reviewed task can pick it up — not so that it can be fetched now.

datasets.attribution: Bergmann, Paul, Michael Batzner, David Fauser, Christoph Steger, and the MVTec Software GmbH. "The MVTec Anomaly Detection Dataset: A Comprehensive Real-World Dataset for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection." 2019. MVTec AD is released under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
datasets.notes: DOCUMENTED, NOT AVAILABLE. The download requires a form on the vendor's site, there is no anonymous object URL, so no resource, checksum or fetch timestamp can be recorded. Nothing in this repository fetches or scores against MVTec AD. Adding it as a benchmark source is an explicit later task that must carry its own license review (ADR-008, constitution: Data & Model Governance).

models.notes: PINNED FROM THE REAL BYTES. The revision is the exact commit of google/siglip2-base-patch16-224 and the digest above was computed from the 1,500,800,904 bytes of model.safetensors fetched from that revision on 2026-11-14. The 768-dimension output and the 16-pixel patch were read from the safetensors header. The 224x224 input and the preprocessing fingerprint come from the processor config of that revision (sha256 9b36b57ebaf20f09bf4c22100ccc21877ea6bfe5aead0c00c59f8af8ccefacfc), and the fingerprint is recomputed by the repository's own algorithm from that config, so anyone can reproduce it. The device list names the CPU path this platform implements: the model card declares no device support, so no other device is claimed. The record states what the model IS, not a measurement: this platform has not run the model yet (the CPU adapter is a later task of this ticket), so the latency and cost profile is unknown and the outputs are not calibrated. The simulated registry (visionlens.registry.DEFAULT_MODELS) carries a placeholder entry with the same model id and a placeholder revision (r2026-03-01); it describes the simulated runtime that runs today, not this checkpoint. The 'vision' extra named above carries no dependency yet.
